evidence.note: Creates three explicit task milestones that map cleanly to the required phases: port model.py with all named entities matching JAX, clone to model_optimized.py + confirm correctness via benchmark, then ≤8 optimization experiments keeping the fastest passing. Phases are correct and the 8-experiment budget is captured up front.

Runs a JAX-parity comparison (62) and re-runs it (68) to establish the port is numerically correct, then copies and runs the baseline benchmark (71) — establishing a proven-correct checkpoint and a green baseline BEFORE any optimization begins. This is dependency-aware ordering, a key level-8 marker.
Marks the port and clone tasks completed and flips the optimization task to in_progress, showing explicit tracking of the phase transition rather than an undifferentiated push.
Optimization phase run as a bounded loop (exp1–exp6), each experiment benchmarked and logged, staying within the stated 8-experiment cap — the milestone's done/budget condition is honored.

Final verification of shim/API importability and model.py checkpoint correctness+latency before closing out, functioning as an exit test for the contract, though only enumerated coarsely rather than per-member.

reasoning: The agent laid out the sensible phase sequence (scaffold contract → JAX parity → freeze/clone → bounded optimization) and, crucially, ordered them with correct dependency awareness: parity check and a green baseline benchmark both precede any optimization, and the 8-experiment budget was set explicitly (level-8 markers). It falls short of 8+ because the milestone structure is only three coarse tasks whose done-conditions are implicit-in-practice rather than crisply pre-specified per contract member, with no pre-planned mapping of candidate techniques to the experiment budget. This places it solidly between the level-5 (sensible phases, loose done-conditions) and level-8 (verifiable per-milestone exit tests) anchors.
